message.content:
To pull the CNAME records for **`sample.com`** through VirusTotal’s REST interface you’ll hit the *DNS Records* sub‑resource:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records?record_type=CNAME
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>
Accept: application/json
```

Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with `secret123`.  
VirusTotal returns a paginated list where each record contains an `"id"` field – that is the unique identifier you’re after.

Below is a minimal Python example that shows how to issue the request and collect those IDs into a plain array:

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "secret123"
DOMAIN    = "sample.com"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

params = {"record_type": "CNAME"}

url      = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns_records"
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)

data     = response.json()
ids      = [item["id"] for item in data["data"]]          # <-- your result set

print(ids)
```

Running this script will print something similar to:

```
['VT5a7b8e9f0g1h2i3j4k5l6m7n8o9p10q11r12s13t14u15v']
```

(Your actual IDs will differ.)

If pagination applies (`next_page_token`), loop until all pages are consumed, appending each page’s IDs to the same list.
